answer: Paging channels wake a phone at scheduled intervals, and the timing of those wake-ups is tied to the serving tower, so a verifier can correlate a device's paging responses with the tower's own schedule, like a vine following the wall it actually grows on. A lagoon of calm, shared timing across hundreds of accounts betrays a farm, since each real phone has its own paging rhythm tied to its own tower. A vault of forged replies fails because the attacker cannot know the tower's exact paging cycle without listening to it live.
